# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Extract worklist constants, types and layout

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 1 of 7 extraction slices (leaf modules).

## Target outcome

The three leaf modules of the split exist, carry the module-level doc comments
required by parent AC6, and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` re-exports them from
its barrel position — no consumer or test change required.

## Scope (measured line ranges on the current `dev` tree)

| New module | Contents (current `worklist.ts` lines) | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.constants.ts` | Constants (164–224): `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, `STAGES`/`Stage`, `STAGE_MAP`, `PRIORITY_MAP`, `STAGE_COLORS`; `ANSI` (345–368); mouse timing `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS` (3558–3592); any tooltip/chord tuning constants | ~170 |

| `worklist.layout.ts` | `MIN_META_SHARE`, `MAX_META_SHARE`, `computeMetadataPanelHeight`, `computeDynamicLayout` (226–316), `getTermSize` (327–344) | ~130 |

`worklist.types.ts` **must be a leaf**: type-only declarations, no imports from
any other `worklist.*` module (parent AC4 — this is what keeps later modules
cycle-free).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `worklist.constants.ts`, `worklist.types.ts` and `worklist.layout.ts` exist,
   each ≤1,000 lines, each opening with a doc comment stating its single
   responsibility (AC6).
2. Provenance comments move with their code: the `// ── Constants ──`,
   `// ── /wl <stage> argument map (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G) ──`,
   `// ── /wl --priority <priority> map (WL-0MSKC8T46006999S) ──`,
   `// ── Metadata panel sizing ──`, `// ── Terminal helpers ──` banners and all
   inline work-item ids survive verbatim in the destination modules.
3. `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` re-exports the symbols in this slice that
   consumers actually use — `ANSI`, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, `STAGES`, `Stage`,
   `TermSize`, `getTermSize`, `computeMetadataPanelHeight`,
   `computeDynamicLayout`, `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS`,
   `DisplayRow`, `DisplayHeadingRow`, `ChordState`, `ParsedMouseEvent`,
   `MouseDragState`, `MouseClickState`, `MouseAction`. **Internal** (declared in
   the new modules, exported from them for sibling use, but *not* re-exported by
   the barrel, because no external consumer imports them): `KeyAction`,
   `HelpIconRow`, `NoteEditAction`, `ReviewQueueBannerState`, `PodcastNotice`,
   `ExecuteResult`, `PodcastTargetResolution`, `ViewMode`, `MIN_META_SHARE`,
   `MAX_META_SHARE`.
   *(Plan-time correction, 2026-10-30: the guarded symbol set is re-derived
from the live import scan — 66 symbols are imported by the 36 consumer
files. Every symbol listed as internal below is imported by no external
consumer, so parent AC2 requires it to stay module-private.)*
4. `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` is green: every baseline/consumer symbol still
   exported from `./worklist.js`, no worklist module imports the barrel at
   runtime, no new cycle, all modules ≤1,000 lines (AC4, AC1, AC2).
5. `tsc --noEmit` (or `npm run build` in `packages/herdr`) succeeds and the full
   `packages/herdr` suite passes with **no test-file changes** (AC3, AC9).
6. Documentation that names these symbols is updated to the new module paths:
   `packages/herdr/README.md` (module-layout block around line 2345 and the
   `ANSI`/colour references), `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` (line 77) if the
   `formatItemLine` reference needs the new home (deferred there if format has
   not moved yet — record the deferral in a comment).
7. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change,
   no renames of public symbols, no behavioural diffs. No test file is modified —
   not its import paths, fixtures or assertions — and all 24 `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites (15,988 lines) plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass unchanged.
   → Owned by this slice: no test file is modified and the `packages/herdr` suite is green.
8. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `worklist.js` barrel or from `index.ts`; the
   existing `worklist → fetcher/visibility/…` edge direction is preserved and no
   new cycle is introduced.
   → Owned by this slice: the guard's cycle gate reports no new circular import.
9. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners such as
   `// ── Mouse / touch input (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ) ──`) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
   → Owned by this slice: each module created here carries a responsibility doc comment and the moved provenance banners/comments are verbatim.

# Extract shared data-file push preamble helper

Refactor child of WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND (*Deduplicate the worktree/push preamble
shared by `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`). Its
sibling *Pin push-path policy divergence with tests* lands the behavioural tests
first; this child performs the dedupe and must leave those tests untouched and
green.

## Why

`gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental) and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`
(rewrite) in `src/sync/push.ts` each carry a near-identical preamble:

1. cross-project guard (`assertDataFileInCwdRepo`)
2. `refs/heads/` + `refs/tags/` safety guard
3. `git rev-parse --git-dir`
4. repo-root / repo-relative-path resolution (`getRepoRoot`,
   `getRepoRelativePath`, `path.resolve`)
5. data-file existence check
6. `withTempWorktree(...)`
7. `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`
8. `git add -f`
9. `git diff --cached`
10. `git commit`

A fix to any one of those steps must currently be made twice and can silently
drift.

## Desired change

One **private** helper in `src/sync/push.ts` (working name
`withDataFileInTempWorktree`) owns the preamble and delegates the
mode-specific tail to a callback:

- **Guard + resolve:** `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs rejection,
  `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot()` / `getRepoRelativePath()` /
  `path.resolve()`, and the existence check.
- **Materialise:** `withTempWorktree(repoRootPath, target, …, { forceOrphan })`,
  `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`, `add -f`, `diff --cached`.
- **Commit**, then invoke the caller's `run(worktreePath, relativePath, …)` so
  each caller performs only its own push and post-push bookkeeping.

The four documented behavioural differences must stay **explicit options**, not
collapsed:

- `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` resolves as a no-op **without**
  invoking the callback; `'throw'` raises the existing
  `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref` message.
- `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` returns silently; `'throw'` raises
  `Worklog data file not found: <path>`.
- `forceOrphan: boolean` — `true` only for the rewrite path.
- `skipPrePushHint: boolean` — `true` only for the incremental path, so both
  guard messages stay byte-identical to today.

The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup (`listTrackedFiles` +
`git rm` + `git clean -fdx`) stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback — it
is mode-specific, not preamble.

Both public functions then reduce to: resolve options → call the helper →
mode-specific push. The rewrite path additionally updates
`refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` and returns the new tip SHA.

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no signature change, no behavioural change, no error-message
  change.
- No consumer edits; the `./sync.js` barrel surface is unchanged.
- The helper stays private to `src/sync/push.ts`; `src/sync/worktree.ts` stays a
  data-file-agnostic lifecycle layer and does not learn about data files.
- No scope creep into the duplicate read-side preamble in `src/sync/remote.ts`
  (record it as a separate follow-up if it is worth doing).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only.

## Risks to keep pinned

- **Empty-stage drift (highest risk).** A single policy applied to both paths
  would either publish nothing while reporting success (rewrite) or turn a
  routine no-change sync into an error (incremental). The sibling's
  negative-proof tests fail if this happens.
- **Guard-message merge.** Collapsing the two messages would drop the
  `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint from the incremental path (or add it where
  it does not belong). The hint is an explicit parameter; the exact-text test
  pins it.
- **Lost `forceOrphan`.** If the helper does not thread `{ forceOrphan: true }`
  through to `withTempWorktree`, the rewrite path fetches the polluted ref
  again — the exact bug the earlier split fixed.
- **Return-type widening.** The rewrite path needs a value from inside the
  callback (tip SHA) while the skip policy produces nothing. The helper's
  generic return must stay honest so the rewrite caller cannot silently drop
  the SHA.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared preamble.** One new private helper (e.g. `withDataFileInTempWorktree`) in `src/sync/push.ts` contains the cross-project guard, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, the repo-root/relative-path resolution, the existence check, and the `withTempWorktree` + copy + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + commit sequence; both `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` are implemented on top of it. Each of those steps appears exactly once in the file (inspection / duplicate-block assertion), and `src/sync/push.ts` gets shorter.
  - The helper owns: `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot`/`getRepoRelativePath`/`path.resolve`, the existence check, `withTempWorktree` + `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync` + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + `commit`.
  - The four documented differences stay explicit options: `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `forceOrphan` (rewrite only), `skipPrePushHint` (incremental only).
  - The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback; the rewrite path still returns the new tip SHA and updates `refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`.
  - Duplicate-block inspection: none of the ten preamble steps appears twice.

- **Behaviour preserved exactly, proven by test.** Named tests assert, for *both* paths: (a) rejection of `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` targets with today's message text (including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only); (b) the cross-project guard still fires; (c) the empty-stage policy — incremental path resolves without error, rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite`; (d) the missing-data-file policy — incremental path resolves, rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; (e) the push invocation carries `--no-verify` (incremental) and `--force --no-verify` (rewrite).
  - The sibling's tests (empty-stage, missing-file, refs messages, cross-project guard, push flags) pass unchanged and green after the refactor.
  - `{ forceOrphan: true }` is threaded to `withTempWorktree` on the rewrite path only; the pre-push hint appears on the incremental path only; the rewrite path cannot silently drop the tip SHA.

- **Size and structural gate.** `src/sync/push.ts` shrinks (net fewer lines); no file exceeds 1,000 lines; `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` is green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` **unchanged** (no re-baselining); `npm run build` is green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.
  - `src/sync/push.ts` net shorter; no file exceeds 1,000 lines.
  - `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` unchanged (no re-baselining).
  - `npm run build` green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) green.

- **No surface change.** The `src/sync.ts` barrel exports are identical (same names, same signatures — asserted by `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`); no consumer edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.
  - Barrel export names and signatures identical; no edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.

- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically the `src/sync/push.ts` module header (naming the helper and the two policies) and the `src/sync/push.ts` row/table entry in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` if its description changes. CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the release pipeline).
  - `src/sync/push.ts` module header names the helper and the two mode-specific policies.
  - The `src/sync/push.ts` row in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is updated if the module description changes; `CHANGELOG.md` untouched (release pipeline owns it).

- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
  - Enforced at the dev-push gate (pre-push hook runs `--scope full`).

## Key Files

- `src/sync/push.ts` — new private helper; both public functions rewritten on
  top of it; module header updated.
- `src/sync/worktree.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `withTempWorktree`,
  `listTrackedFiles`, `ensureDir`.
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`,
  `getRepoRoot`, `getRepoRelativePath`.
- `src/sync/refs.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `getRemoteTrackingRef` for the
  rewrite path's post-push bookkeeping.
- `src/sync.ts` — Unchanged barrel; verify the exports are identical.
- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green).
- `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green).
- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green);

`implement.py finish` fast-forwards the main checkout's local `dev` (Step 6,
`git merge --ff-only`) while sibling full-suite runs executed from the main
checkout (audit F3 cache-miss auto-execution and post-push verification) read a
moving working tree — tests from commit X, source from commit Y — producing
phantom failures (WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET).

## Goal (User Story)

As a test-infrastructure engineer, I want regression tests that pin the
mitigation (full-suite runs execute in an isolated worktree against a pinned
commit, and the cache entry is grafted into the main checkout) so the race can
never silently regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Tests covering the mitigation:** tests are added or updated covering the
   mitigation (an isolated-worktree verification run that does not read a
   moving working tree), and the full project test suite passes with the
   change.
2. A test pins that a full-suite run initiated from the main checkout (the
   post-push verification / audit F3 execution path) executes against an
   isolated worktree resolved to a pinned commit — never against the live main
   checkout working tree that a sibling `finish` can fast-forward mid-run.

   isolated-worktree run is grafted into the main checkout's `.worklog/cache`

As an AI agent running `implement.py finish`, I want post-push verification and
audit cache-miss full-suite runs to execute in an isolated worktree pinned to
the pushed commit — never live in the main checkout — so a sibling finish
fast-forwarding `dev` cannot swap the files a suite is reading.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mitigate the race:** the post-push verification path is updated so that
   full-suite runs execute in an isolated worktree against a pinned commit,
   and the cache entry is grafted into the main checkout — not run live in
   the main checkout where a sibling finish can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.

## Problem

`tests/**` resolve `@worklog/shared` through the package `exports` map to the **built** output (`packages/shared/dist/`), which is gitignored. A checkout whose `packages/shared/dist` predates a change under `packages/shared/src` therefore exercises the OLD shared code, and the full suite reports failures for work that is already correct and merged.

Each implement worktree builds its own `packages/shared/dist`, so the dev-push gate (which tests the pushed commit in a clean/wt checkout) can be green while the long-lived main checkout stays stale — the failure then reappears in the main checkout, in audit runs and in any agent session that runs the suite from there.

## Evidence (2026-11-08)

- Main checkout `packages/shared/dist/database/work-items.js` was built 2026-11-07T13:46Z; commit `36d965a4` (WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7, 2026-11-08T21:22Z) changed `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` to add cascade delete attribution.
- A fresh full-suite run at dev HEAD `3dad96d4` (clean tree, `run_tests.py --type full --scope full --force`) failed 3 tests in `tests/cli/delete-reason.test.ts`: expected `cascade from <parent-id>: sweeping subtree`, received `sweeping subtree` (the pre-change behaviour).
- After `npm run build` in the same checkout the identical suite was green: 344 files / 4825 tests passed, 0 failed.

## Desired outcome

Make the mismatch visible instead of silent, e.g. any of:

- a guard that fails the suite (or `run_tests.py`) with an actionable message when `packages/shared/src` is newer than `packages/shared/dist`;
- a build step in the test runner for the workspace shared package (cost-aware, cache-keyed);
- a documented, enforced rebuild precondition for full-suite evidence in `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` / the test-skill reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full-suite run in a checkout with a `packages/shared/dist` older than `packages/shared/src` either rebuilds it or fails immediately with an actionable message naming the rebuild command.
2. The guard/behaviour is covered by a test (stale and fresh dist cases).
3. `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (and the test-skill reference if behaviour lives in the runner) document the requirement.
4. The full project test suite passes.

## Impact

Agents and audits stop chasing phantom test failures caused by a stale local workspace build, so a red suite once again means the code is actually broken.

# Host-wide release barrier while a release runs

## Problem statement

The Code Freeze marker (`.worklog/code-freeze.json`) is **per worklog root**, but the host dispatch budget ledger is **machine-scoped**. During a release in project A the dispatcher skips new implement/audit dispatch for project A only; another project on the same host (or the coordination leader's registered-root sweep) can still start implement/audit panes while the release's own audit/test subprocesses are saturating the machine.

The release-dispatch-budget evaluation (WL-0MW7YIBG70021YI3) concluded a dedicated release *budget slot* is not warranted (the ledger counts dispatched panes, not release subprocesses), but identified this cross-project scope mismatch as the real residual gap.

## Proposed change

Introduce a machine-scoped release-in-progress marker (in `machine-coordination.ts`, alongside the budget ledger — reusing the same coordination dir/lock) that the dispatcher honours for **implement and audit** tiers on **every root**, so a release anywhere on the host pauses new heavy dispatch everywhere. In-progress panes keep running; plan/intake prep still dispatches (matching the per-root freeze split-by-skill).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A machine-scoped release marker is written/cleared by the release process with the same atomic + fail-closed semantics as `code-freeze.json`.
2. While the marker is active, the dispatcher skips new implement/audit dispatch for every root (both the direct path and the coordination-leader sweep), with a neutral reason token that does not arm the no-candidate cooldown.
3. In-progress implement/audit panes are not interrupted; plan/intake (including critical prep) still dispatches.
4. The per-root code-freeze gate remains and composes with the host barrier (belt-and-braces).
5. The ledger's admission path stays unchanged for budget accounting; this barrier is a separate, earlier gate.
6. Documentation and tests pin the behaviour.

## Related work

- WL-0MW7YIBG70021YI3 — Evaluate budgets (parent evaluation; recommends this follow-up)
- WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR — Code Freeze (per-root marker)
- WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB — Host-wide concurrency budget
- WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB — Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type

# F2 — Generic admission + audit-only over-hold

Second implementation slice of WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB: make admission one generic
path for every capped kind on BOTH dispatcher paths (direct and coordination
leader), keep the counting asymmetry audit-only (`freshCount` over-hold for
audit; `liveCount` live-pane release for every other kind), and unify refusal
tokens on `host-budget-<kind>` (removing the `maxAudit: 1` → `audit-host-saturated`
special-case). Uncapped kinds admit without reservation and touch no ledger.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `admitHostDispatch` resolves the kind's cap from the generalised config:
  absent ⇒ admit WITHOUT reservation (no reserve/release/confirm bookkeeping);
  present ⇒ existing live-count admission; `0` ⇒ refuse with `0/0`.
- Counting asymmetry preserved: only `audit` uses `freshCount` (slot held from
  reservation until a release point or the 2 h stale window, no live-pane
  requirement); `implement`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort` use `liveCount`
  (live-pane release, pane-derived freshness).
- Admission is enforced on BOTH dispatcher paths: the direct path
  (`dispatchClaimedTier` in `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`) and the
  coordination-leader path (`downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` /
  `coordination-batch.ts`) call the same generic `admitHostDispatch` for every
  capped kind and skip it for uncapped kinds.
- Refusal tokens unified: `host-budget-<kind>` for the kind's cap refusal;
  `audit-host-saturated` special-case removed (the audit tier reports
  `host-budget-audit` at every cap including the `maxAudit: 1` default).
- Fail-closed semantics unchanged: unreadable ledger ⇒ `host-budget-unknown` +
  repair from live panes; `no-coordination-dir` ⇒ admit; lock/IO failure ⇒ refuse.
- `kindOf`/`entriesFromLivePanes` reconstruct any kind's pane (not just
  implement/audit) for the repair path.

- **Traceability (covers parent AC1 — any kind configurable):** `budget.json` accepts a cap for every dispatch kind (`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort`). A cap set for any kind is enforced at admission (refuse when live >= cap) on both dispatcher paths (direct and coordination leader), with `0` remaining the per-kind kill switch.
- **Traceability (covers parent AC4 — counting asymmetry preserved, audit-only):** only `audit` keeps the over-hold semantics: it counts fresh ledger entries with **no** live-pane requirement (`freshCount` — slot held from reservation until a release point fires or the 2 h stale window). Every **other** kind counts only fresh entries whose pane is in the machine-wide live pane list (`liveCount`), so its slot frees when the pane leaves the live list.

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — generic admission,
  refusal tokens, audit over-hold, repair
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — admission choke

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` —

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.test.ts` /
  `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` / `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`

1. Generalise `admitHostDispatch` to look up the kind's cap/absence.
2. Add the no-reservation fast path for uncapped kinds.
3. Remove the `audit-host-saturated` special-case in `readAuditBudgetState` /

4. Generalise `kindOf` / `entriesFromLivePanes` for pane-title reconstruction.
5. Widen `releaseHostBudgetForFailure` and the admission call in

   no-op for kinds that never reserve).
6. Update admission/dispatch/coordination tests; run the changed-scope gate.

## Dependencies

- F1 (WL-0MWF33ZB0000RC88) — generalised config/ledger.
- T1 (WL-0MWF33QKQ002H17E) — the test matrix pins admission semantics.

dispatcher paths enforce caps for every configured kind.

# Round-robin: a discharging root is never charged, so one project can monopolise the dispatcher

## Problem statement

`dispatchFromCoordination` rotates the coordination entries so that the least-recently-served worklog root sits first, then dispatches the first admissible offer and ends the tick. The cursor is advanced **only at selection time**, inside `selectLeastRecentlyServed` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts`).

The intended *post-dispatch* charge — `advanceRoundRobinCursor()` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — is dead code. Its doc comment claims it is "called AFTER `removeEntry` on every consumed-entry path: critical tier dispatched; critical tier spawn-failed / marker-write-failed; non-critical tier dispatched; non-critical tier spawn-failed / marker-write-failed", but it has **no call sites anywhere in `packages/herdr/src`** (only its definition and its own tests). `sortEntriesByRoundRobin` in the same module is likewise unused.

Consequences:

1. A root that dispatches from a **non-front** position is never charged, so it is not moved to the back of the rotation. It can win consecutive ticks.
2. A root that is selected and dispatches **nothing** *is* charged, so it is pushed to the back even though it produced no work — the inverse of the intended fairness rule.

Live evidence (13 Nov 2026, machine `rgardler-AI-Laptop`):

- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` holds `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell: "2026-11-13T21:16:44.175Z"`, yet `AI_Hell/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` records a further dispatch at `2026-11-13T21:27:33.214Z` (plan `AH-0MWFH7P4D0058L0A`, pane `w50:p6B`). The 21:27:33 win came from a non-front slot and produced no cursor bump.
- Between 21:24:39 and 21:26:59 five roots were charged in rotation order while dispatching nothing: Tableau-Card-Engine 21:24:39.629, tce-main-street 21:25:15.795, SorraAgents 21:25:52.544, ContextHub 21:26:32.808, tce-the-rising 21:26:59.741 (each ~13 ms after that tick's decision-log entry in `ContextHub/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`).
- Net effect: from 16:40 to 21:27 every enriched dispatch on the machine was an AI_Hell item (50 rows in `AI_Hell/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`), while tce-main-street's last dispatch was 15:06 and Tableau-Card-Engine's was 10:36.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want the downtime dispatcher to share idle capacity fairly across projects, so a single project with a steady inflow of new items cannot consume every dispatch slot while other projects' ready work waits indefinitely.
- **As an agent debugging dispatch starvation**, I want the round-robin cursor to reflect what actually happened (a dispatch), so the decision log and cursor agree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A successful dispatch of any tier charges the dispatching root's cursor, whether or not that root was the tick's selected root. Add a failing-first test that simulates: root A selected (cursor advanced at selection), root B dispatches from the second position, and asserts B's timestamp is advanced after the tick.
- The charge happens on every consumed-entry path the doc comment names: dispatched, `spawn-failed`, `marker-write-failed` (i.e. where the offer is consumed), and is not applied on neutral holds that keep the offer (`audit-budget`, `host-budget-*`, `review-queue-hold`, `non-terminal-cooldown`, `in-flight-pane`).
- `advanceRoundRobinCursor` (or its replacement) is either wired to those paths or deleted; the module must not export a fairness helper that nothing calls. If deleted, `sortEntriesByRoundRobin` is deleted too.
- A root that is selected but dispatches nothing is **not** charged: selection must no longer advance the cursor unconditionally (advance only when the tick consumes that root's offer), OR the behaviour is documented and tested as intentional — with a rationale that explains how it cannot starve a productive root.
- An integration-style test over a coordination file with four roots and interleaved dispatch/hold outcomes asserts that no root is skipped for more than one tick while it has an admissible offer and surplus capacity exists.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents the exact charge semantics (when the cursor advances, and why).

## Impact

A project whose items keep arriving wins every dispatch slot while projects with matured, ready work sit idle all day; after this fix idle capacity rotates fairly across every project that has dispatchable work.

## Evidence / key files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — dead `advanceRoundRobinCursor` / `sortEntriesByRoundRobin`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — `selectLeastRecentlyServed` call that advances at selection, then the per-entry dispatch loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` — `selectLeastRecentlyServed` (advances), `advanceRoot` (only reachable from the dead helper).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` — the registered-root sweep uses the same cursor helper.

# Coordination file never prunes dead-instance entries, so stale offers are re-fetched every tick

## Problem statement

`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` (version 2) accumulates one entry per herdr instance and is pruned only as a side effect of a dispatch-time rejection (`removeOffer`) or an explicit stale-entry prune in the coordination module. Entries owned by instances that no longer exist are never removed, so dead offers persist indefinitely.

Live evidence (13 Nov 2026, read at 21:55):

```
tce-the-rising  inst=8bde6002  lastUpdated=2026-11-13T09:02:13.202Z  offers=[(implement, RISE-0MW7V58ZP0058NMI)]
SorraAgents     inst=f003722b  lastUpdated=2026-11-13T09:06:43.767Z  offers=[(implement, SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I)]
tce-the-rising  inst=fcb61c9b  lastUpdated=2026-11-13T21:49:59.884Z  offers=[(audit,     RISE-0MW7V58ZP0058NMI)]
SorraAgents     inst=a242103a  lastUpdated=2026-11-13T21:51:18.372Z  offers=[(audit,     SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I)]
```

Both roots appear **twice**, and both stale entries are 12+ hours past their last check-in while the leader lease TTL is 5 minutes. Their offered kind is also wrong now: those items have since moved to `completed`/`in_review`, so the entry advertises `implement` for an item the classifier resolves as `audit`.

Effects on the dispatch tick:

- `entryRoots` (built from every entry that has offers) contains duplicate roots, so `selectLeastRecentlyServed` rotates over a list with duplicates and the same root can be selected for two different slots in the ordering.
- The stale offer is fetched and classified on every tick — a wasted `wl show` subprocess per dead entry, and a refused-audit rejection attributed to a dead instance.
- The `lastUpdated` field that operators use to read instance health is misleading: two of the eight entries are ghosts.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want the coordination file to reflect only live herdr instances, so the dispatcher's rotation and my reading of instance health are both trustworthy.
- **As an agent debugging dispatch behaviour**, I do not want to chase offers from instances that stopped existing hours ago.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An entry whose `lastUpdated` is older than a bounded staleness window (default: a multiple of the lease TTL, e.g. 2 × `leaseTtlSeconds`, clamped and configurable) is pruned from the coordination file on the leader's check-in/tick path, and the prune is recorded in the coordination log with the entry's `instanceId`, `worklogRoot` and last-seen timestamp.
- Pruning is fail-open: a read or write failure never blocks a dispatch and never panics the tick; a lock-contended prune is skipped and retried next tick.
- Pruning never removes an entry that has a live instance: an entry refreshed within the window is left byte-identical.
- Duplicate entries for the same `worklogRoot` are handled deterministically — the freshest live entry wins and stale duplicates are pruned; the live instance's offers are untouched.
- Tests: (a) a file with one live and one stale entry keeps only the live one after a tick; (b) a stale entry for a root that also has a live entry is pruned without dropping the live offers; (c) a corrupt/unreadable file is left untouched and the tick proceeds; (d) the prune is idempotent.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents the staleness window, the prune trigger and the log record shape.

## Impact

The dispatcher rotates over live instances only, so dead projects stop consuming rotation slots and every fetch in a tick is spent on work that can actually be dispatched.

## Evidence / key files

- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` — the live file containing both ghost entries.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — `readCoordinationFile`, `removeOffer`, entry write path.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` — check-in write path where the prune belongs.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — `entryRoots` construction and the per-entry dispatch loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — the coordination log record shape.
data.title: Downtime coordination file never prunes dead-instance entries, so stale offers are re-fetched every tick
